subject: CSQ: storage locality and end-of-life handling for Hosted API
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@lumenix.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: security@lumenix.com
Date: 2026-09-14 09:22 PDT
Subject: Customer security questionnaire — storage locality, retention, and deletion (hosted API)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking our security questionnaire. We have a few specific follow-ups on the Hosted API data lifecycle that are blockers for Procurement. Can you confirm the following details so we can move to the next internal review?

1) Data residency: When a customer selects a primary region for the Hosted API (e.g., us-west-2), where are request payloads, model outputs, and any derived artifacts (embeddings, logs) stored by default? Are copies created in other regions or for DR?

2) Retention: What are your default retention windows for:
   - Request/response payloads associated with customer API keys
   - System/operation logs and traces
   - Embeddings and derived artifacts

3) Deletion and proof: If Lumenix requests a purge for a tenant, what is the expected SLA (hours/days) for complete deletion from primary stores and from backups/snapshots? Do you provide attestations or an audit log showing deletion events?

4) Backups & snapshots: How long are automatic backups/snapshots retained, and are they geo-replicated? If geo-replicated, can you guarantee they remain within the customer-specified region or country?

5) Encryption & key management: Are data-at-rest keys tenant-specific, and do you support bringing your own key (BYOK)?

If you can attach a short appendix or a single-page summary we can include with our RFI that would be ideal.

Best,
Elaine Park
Head of Information Security
Lumenix Therapeutics
security@lumenix.com

[Attachment: Lumenix_CSQ_2026.xlsx (referenced)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@lumenix.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-15 08:45 PDT
Subject: Re: Customer security questionnaire — storage locality, retention, and deletion (hosted API)

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. I answered inline below and attached a short appendix (hosted-data-geography-appendix.pdf) with diagrams. Happy to hop on a quick call if you want us to walk through anything.

1) Data residency:
- Primary stores: All customer request payloads, generated outputs (model response text), and derived artifacts (embeddings, reranking artifacts) are stored in customer-specific tenant buckets within the chosen cloud region by default.
- Copies: We do not proactively copy tenant customer data to other regions for normal operation. For cross-region failover cases we keep immutable snapshots only when a customer opts into multi-region DR. Those snapshots are created only after an explicit configuration change and are subject to the customer's region restrictions.

2) Retention (default settings; can be configured per-tenant):
- Request/response payloads: default 30 days (retention window used for quality monitoring and model improvement pipeline opt-in). Customers can reduce to 0 days or opt out of persistence entirely for API keys tied to ephemeral mode.
- System logs/traces: 90 days for operational debugging; sensitive fields are redacted on ingest and full request bodies are not included unless the customer opts in.
- Embeddings/derived artifacts: 90 days by default when generated by the Hosted API; for long-term storage customers can opt-in to archival; otherwise they follow the embedding retention window.

3) Deletion and proof:
- Primary deletion SLA: When we receive an authenticated tenant erasure request via the Console or support channel, primary-store deletion is initiated within 24 hours and typically completes within 72 hours for typical dataset sizes.
- Backup/snapshot deletion: Snapshots are marked for deletion within 72 hours of the request and removed during the next scheduled snapshot compaction cycle (up to 30 days depending on snapshot cadence).
- Attestation/audit: We can provide an audit record with timestamps for the deletion request, the deletion job run, and the confirmation when object manifests are garbage-collected. For enterprise customers we include those deletion events in the audit logs delivered via the Console and can provide a signed attestation PDF on request.

4) Backups & snapshots:
- Retention: Automatic backups are retained for 30–90 days depending on the product tier; backup retention and snapshot cadence are configurable for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Geo-replication: Backups are not geo-replicated by default. For customers who require geo-redundancy we implement cross-region snapshots only with explicit customer consent and configuration. Those cross-region copies are restricted to named regions in the customer's account agreement; we do not move customer-managed encrypted backups outside those agreed regions.

5) Encryption & key management:
- Data-at-rest: All customer data is encrypted at rest using KMS-managed keys.
- Tenant-specific keys: For Hosted API, we support customer-specific keys via our KMS integration (separate keys per customer project where requested).
- BYOK: We support BYOK for enterprise customers through our KMS/HSM partner integrations; we can provide implementation notes in the appendix.

Attachments: hosted-data-geography-appendix.pdf (short diagram + summary)

Next steps: Ben will coordinate a short technical call to share architecture diagrams if you want deeper detail on backups and snapshot compaction.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Security & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference
T: 415-555-0123

[Attachment: hosted-data-geography-appendix.pdf]

From: Elaine Park <elaine@lumenix.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: security@lumenix.com
Date: 2026-09-16 10:11 PDT
Subject: Re: Customer security questionnaire — storage locality, retention, and deletion (hosted API)

Thanks Tessa — that's helpful. A couple of clarifying follow-ups before we close with Procurement:

- For the backup/snapshot deletion window you mentioned "up to 30 days" during compaction. Can you confirm whether we can negotiate a shorter maximum (for our contract) and whether Redwood will provide a guaranteed maximum time to full removal from any immutable snapshot stores?
- For encryption: Can you confirm whether snapshot copies are re-encrypted with customer keys when BYOK is enabled, or are they stored using Redwood-managed encryption and only access-controlled by the customer key?
- For audit: Is the deletion attestation a machine-readable audit log (JSON) we can ingest to our SIEM, or is it only provided as a signed PDF?

If it's easier, send the contract-friendly bullets we can paste into the SOW.

-Appreciate it,
Elaine

Subject: Re: Customer security questionnaire — storage locality, retention, and deletion (hosted API)

Hi Elaine — quick follow-up with contract-friendly bullets and a small clarification on backups. Attaching "data-handling-appendix.pdf" and a machine-friendly retention matrix (snapshot-retention-matrix.csv). Ben, please schedule the tech call and add architecture slides.

Contract-friendly bullets (feel free to paste into SOW):
- Data residency: Customer primary data (request payloads, outputs, derived artifacts) will be stored in the cloud region selected at onboarding. Redwood will not replicate primary customer data to other regions without explicit customer configuration.
- Snapshots/backups: Redwood will only create cross-region snapshots for Disaster Recovery when explicitly configured by the customer. Cross-region snapshots are restricted to the regions enumerated in the customer's service agreement.
- Deletion SLA: Redwood will initiate tenant data deletion within 24 hours of a validated request; primary-store deletion will complete within 72 hours in normal cases. Deletion from immutable snapshots will be scheduled within 30 days of request unless otherwise negotiated in the SOW.
- Proof & audit: Redwood will provide machine-readable audit events (JSON) for deletion requests and job completion which can be exported to customer SIEM. For enterprise customers Redwood can also provide a signed attestation upon completion.
- Encryption: When BYOK is enabled, all new snapshots/backups are encrypted using the customer's key material. Existing snapshots created prior to BYOK enablement may require a migration process; Redwood will support a migration plan as part of onboarding.

If you want tighter deletion guarantees (e.g., max 7-day snapshot purge) we can include that as a contractual SLA with an associated fee; Ben and I can include options in the SOW.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Customer Security & Compliance (acting)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: data-handling-appendix.pdf, snapshot-retention-matrix.csv
